content.text:
View A represents four distinct objects: an upper green circle, a right red triangle, a lower blue square, and a left yellow cross. Attention is currently allocated almost entirely to the left yellow cross; the lower blue square and the upper green circle are remembered next-most robustly, the right red triangle least. If you issue a command to select a specific location in view A, the system reliably shifts selection to that commanded location, so you can make any one object immediately available by directing attention there; recoverability for an object after switching is moderate and declines over subsequent steps without resampling.

View B also represents four objects: an upper green triangle, a right red circle, a lower blue square, and a left yellow cross. Attention is currently focused on the left yellow cross; the upper green triangle and right red circle are the next more available, the lower blue square least. However, commands in view B tend to drive attention toward the upper location regardless of which location is requested, so you have limited control to make other locations immediately dominant. Redirecting attention in B will most likely make the upper object become available rather than reliably making any chosen object available.
